subject: sociology
title: Beliefs & Secularisation: The Thesis
welcome_lead: Bruce and Wilson argue religion is fading. The data is mostly with them.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology secularisation Bruce Wilson UK religiosity decline.
final_note: Britain has secularised on every official measure.

concepts.def: Religion's social significance declines with modernity.
Inner faith claims — measured by surveys.
Religion in Secular Society — landmark UK secularisation work.
God Is Dead — defended thesis against critics.

walkthroughs.body_html: Church of England Sunday attendance fell from 40% in 1851 to ~5% in 2010 (Crockett & Voas). 2021 UK census: 46% Christian (down from 72% in 2001); 37% no religion (up from 15% in 2001). Baptisms, marriages and confirmations all in long-term decline.

Wilson (1966): secularisation is the process by which religious institutions, practices and beliefs lose social significance. UK religion has differentiated from state, education and welfare. Religion may persist privately but cannot direct society as before.

Bruce (2002) 'God Is Dead': three causes of decline — social differentiation, societalisation, rationalisation. Believing without belonging is declining belief, not stable. Resists 'spiritual revolution' claims as exaggerated.
